_note: Lane-cited dictionary entries — standard classical Arabic meanings for high-frequency JA tokens in Saadia's Tafsir. Hand-curated against the corpus; not auto-generated. `source: "lane"` means "this is the standard classical Arabic sense, for which Lane's Lexicon is the canonical English reference" — entries paraphrase, they are not verbatim Lane quotes. For Saadia-specific or Blau-divergent senses, see data/tafsir-divergence.json. For tribute and Blau-citation policy, see /about/blau.
_source: Lane's Lexicon (E.W. Lane, An Arabic-English Lexicon, 1863-1893; public domain). Roots verified against the Perseus TEI edition at ~/Tools/arabic-lexicon/lane-xml.
_scope: Hand-curated 2026-05-21; first batch ≈70 entries focused on top-frequency tokens from the Bereshit-Devarim corpus that are NOT in tafsir-divergence.json. Inflected surface forms (suffixed prepositions, fa-prefixed perfects) included where they appear ≥100x in the corpus to improve tap-to-define UX without yet extending the prefix/suffix-stripping logic in lib/lookup.ts.

entries.saadia_note: Saadia's gloss for divine epithets meaning 'God who hears'. Saadia uses 'אלמג'יב' as a divine epithet, often paired with 'אלטאיק' (the All-Capable) in liturgical-prayer contexts within Tafsir.

entries.gloss_en: (the) All-Capable, the One Who Has Power
entries.saadia_note: Saadia's divine-name rendering, esp. paired with אלכאפי for Hebrew אֵל שַׁדַּי. Component of Saadia's compound divine name 'אלטאיק אלכאפי' (the All-Capable, the Sufficient) — his rendering of Hebrew אֵל שַׁדַּי. See the divergence cards on Bereshit 17 for context.
Saadia's divine-name rendering — see טאיק.
Saadia's gloss for Hebrew מֵעַל and עַל in 'over/above' senses.
Saadia's gloss for Hebrew נְחֹשֶׁת.
Saadia's gloss for Hebrew נָדִיב and נִכְבָּד.

entries.notes: Broken plural of שריף. Add as standalone lemma so the bare form resolves outside the divergence-card flow.
entries.saadia_note: Saadia's gloss for Hebrew בְּנֵי הָאֱלֹהִים in Gen 6 — the 'sons of the noble class'. Already discussed under tafsir-divergence (Gen 6:2, 6:4: 'sons-of-the-nobility' for בני האלהים).

entries.notes: Form VIII (reflexive-derived) of خ-ي-ر 'good/excellent' → 'to pick the best'.
entries.saadia_note: Saadia's gloss for Hebrew בָּחַר. See the divergence card for אכ'תיאר (Gen 4:7) for the noun/abstract form.
Saadia's gloss for Hebrew קָרָא in 'call' and 'read' senses. Direct Saadia rendering of Hebrew קָרָא — the cognate carries over.

entries.notes: Heavy in Exodus 27-38.
entries.saadia_note: Saadia's gloss for Hebrew קֶלַע — the courtyard hangings of the Tabernacle. Persian-origin loanword in Arabic, used by Saadia for the screen-fabric panels of the Tabernacle courtyard.
Saadia's gloss for Hebrew שִׁטִּים — the wood of the Tabernacle.

entries.gloss_en: weight; weighing; (as verb wazana) he weighed-out
entries.saadia_note: Saadia's gloss for Hebrew שָׁקַל and מִשְׁקָל.

entries.gloss_en: the (definite article); (as standalone) the article in isolation, typically a citation form or break in text
entries.notes: Normally proclitic: prefixes onto a noun. The standalone form is rare and usually a citation or text break.
Denominative imperfect built on the adjective נגס 'unclean' (see the נגס entry). High-frequency in Vayikra purity laws.
entries.saadia_note: Saadia's denominative of nájisun 'unclean'.
Saadia's gloss for Hebrew מָצָא.
Saadia's gloss for Hebrew תּוֹלַעַת שָׁנִי — the scarlet/crimson tabernacle thread.

entries.notes: Persian asmān 'sky' + gūn 'color' → 'sky-colored'.
entries.saadia_note: Saadia's gloss for Hebrew תְּכֵלֶת. Saadia's signature rendering of the tabernacle's blue thread.
Saadia's gloss for Hebrew הָרַג and הִכָּה לְמָוֶת.

entries.gloss_en: time, point-in-time, appointed-moment; (broken pl. awqāt) times
entries.notes: The bare singular waqt — companion to the existing אוקאת (the broken plural).
entries.saadia_note: Saadia uses both.

entries.notes: Compound of demonstrative ها 'behold' + 1sg pronoun אנא.
entries.saadia_note: Saadia's gloss for Hebrew הִנֵּנִי and הִנֵּה אֲנִי. Saadia's rendering of Hebrew הִנֵּנִי.
Saadia's gloss for Hebrew סָפַר, פָּקַד, נָשָׂא אֶת רֹאשׁ in census contexts.

entries.gloss_en: petty chief, lesser leader (diminutive of raʾīs)
entries.notes: Diminutive of رئيس 'chief'.
entries.saadia_note: Saadia's nuanced rendering of secondary tribal-leadership terms. Saadia uses this form to differentiate junior leadership (e.g. heads of sub-clans) from the principal נשיא.
Saadia's gloss for Hebrew עָנָן.
in Saadia — used for circumcision-covenant community contexts. Saadia uses millah (and its derivatives) in contexts of religious-community identity; appears in covenant-circumcision narratives.
Saadia's gloss for Hebrew אָכַל.
Saadia's gloss for Hebrew אֹכֶל.
Saadia's gloss for Hebrew טָהוֹר.
Saadia's gloss for Hebrew רָם and גָּבוֹהַּ.
Saadia's gloss for Hebrew רָצוֹן and לְרָצוֹן in offering contexts.
Saadia's gloss for Hebrew כֵּלִים in cultic-utensil contexts.
Saadia's gloss for Hebrew עַתּוּד — Hebrew form retained.

Saadia's gloss for Hebrew אֲדוֹנִי in human-respect contexts; NOT for the divine Name. Saadia uses סייד for human masters and respected superiors (e.g. אדני in interpersonal contexts). For the divine Name יהוה Saadia uses אללה.
Saadia's divine-name rendering in some contexts; mostly an epithet. An Arabic divine epithet (also in the Qurʾan, Surat al-Ikhlāṣ); Saadia uses it sparingly in his theological prose.
Saadia's gloss for Hebrew יְאֹר and פִּישׁוֹן. Geographic identification long established in Saadia: יְאֹר (and elsewhere פִּישׁוֹן) = the Nile.

entries.notes: Form IV (causative) of qāma 'to stand'.
entries.saadia_note: Saadia's gloss for Hebrew הֵקִים. Saadia's regular rendering of the Hebrew hiphil הֵקִים.
Saadia's gloss for Hebrew נָשִׂיא.

entries.gloss_en: Lot (Abraham's nephew; father of Moab and Ammon)
Abimelech (king of Gerar / Philistia in Gen 20-21, 26)
Rebecca (Isaac's wife; mother of Jacob and Esau)
Nun (father of Joshua, of the tribe of Ephraim)
Joshua (son of Nun; Moses' attendant and successor)
Gershon (firstborn of Levi; the Gershonite clan)
Kohath (second son of Levi; ancestor of Moses, Aaron, Miriam)
Hagar (Sarah's Egyptian handmaid; mother of Ishmael)
Cain (firstborn of Adam; killer of Abel)
entries.notes: Homograph with the Kenite tribal gentilic — context disambiguates.

entries.gloss_en: Abel (second son of Adam, killed by Cain)
Dinah (daughter of Jacob and Leah; Gen 30, 34)
Ephron the Hittite (seller of the Machpelah cave; Gen 23)
Ishmael (son of Abraham and Hagar; ancestor of the Arab nations)
entries.saadia_note: Saadia uses the Arabic form אסמאעיל (Ismāʿīl) throughout the Tafsir for Hebrew יִשְׁמָעֵאל. The Arabic surface form makes the cross-tradition lineage explicit.

entries.gloss_en: Sihon (Amorite king of Heshbon; Num 21, Deut 2-3)
Aram (the Aramaean region of upper Mesopotamia / Syria)
Midian (descendant of Abraham via Keturah; the Midianite people)
Arnon (river forming the southern border of trans-Jordanian Israel)
Jabbok (river east of the Jordan; site of Jacob's wrestling, Gen 32)
Jericho (the lowland city west of the Jordan)
the Red Sea — al-Qulzum, the medieval Arabic name for Hebrew יַם סוּף
entries.notes: Medieval Arabic geographers used al-Qulzum (Clysma, near modern Suez) as the standard name for the entire Red Sea / Gulf of Suez.

entries.gloss_en: Goshen — al-Sadir, the medieval Arabic identification of the Egyptian region where Israel dwelt (Hebrew גֹּשֶׁן)
Gerar — al-Khalus, the medieval Arabic identification of the Philistine city in the western Negev (Hebrew גְּרָר)
the Euphrates — al-Furāt, the standard Arabic name for Hebrew פְּרָת
Mosul — al-Mawṣil, the medieval Arabic identification of biblical אַשּׁוּר (Asshur, region/city in upper Mesopotamia)
Nablus — the medieval Arabic identification of biblical שְׁכֶם (Shechem, the Samaritan city)
Abyssinia / Ethiopia — al-Ḥabash, the medieval Arabic identification of biblical כּוּשׁ (Cush)
Zawila — the medieval Arabic identification of biblical חֲוִילָה (Havilah, the gold-bearing land of Gen 2:11)
Banyas — the medieval Arabic identification of the city of Dan at the headwaters of the Jordan
the Tigris — Dijla, the standard Arabic name for Hebrew חִדֶּקֶל
Qardū — the medieval Arabic/Aramaic identification of biblical אֲרָרָט (Ararat), the mountain range in northern Mesopotamia where Noah's ark rested
entries.notes: Matches the Targum Onqelos rendering and Q11:44.
